  • Method Details

    • loadOnce

      public static void loadOnce(String url, TeaVmScriptLoader.Ok onOk, TeaVmScriptLoader.Err onErr)
      Loads a JS file once. Multiple concurrent calls are coalesced. The state is stored on the global object.

      Every lazily loaded support script comes through here: the stdlib bundles (<lib>.min.js) and also themes.js, emoji.js and openiconic.js, which all have the same problem this method's two host-provided globals solve. They are checked in this order:

      • PLANTUML_STDLIB_LOADER: a function (url, onOk, onErr) that delivers the script's content itself, in whatever way fits the host. For a stdlib bundle it populates PLANTUML_STDLIB / PLANTUML_STDLIB_JSON / PLANTUML_STDLIB_INFO for the library before calling onOk, or calls onErr with a message. Returning false (strictly) declines the URL, and loading proceeds through the script tag as if no hook were set, so a host that only handles stdlib bundles can decline themes.js and friends. The hook is the only way to load these files where a script tag cannot work: a Web Worker (no document), a browser extension that may fetch remote data but not execute remote code, or a non-browser runtime. Mirrors how a host can pre-populate PLANTUML_THEMES for getTheme(String).
      • PLANTUML_STDLIB_BASE: a URL prefix for the script tag, so a page that imports the engine from a CDN can point the loading of all of these files at wherever they are hosted. Without it the URL stays relative, which resolves against the consuming document, not the engine's location.
      A host may instead pre-populate the globals a script would have set and mark __pl_script_state[url] = { state: 'loaded' }; the fast path then skips loading entirely. With neither global set, the behaviour is exactly what it always was.

      public static org.teavm.jso.JSObject getRaw_PLANTUML_STDLIB(String namespace, String path)
      Retrieves the raw lines array for a .puml file from a loaded stdlib library.
      Parameters:
      namespace - the library name (e.g. "aws", "c4")
      path - the relative path within the library (e.g. "compute/ec2")
      Returns:
      the JS array of lines, or null if not found

    • getTheme

      public static String getTheme(String name)
      Retrieves the raw text of a bundled theme, as published by themes.js into the PLANTUML_THEMES map.

      Reads from the global object rather than from window, so that a host which pre-populates PLANTUML_THEMES (on globalThis) can use themes inside a Web Worker, where there is no document to append a script tag to, or in a non-browser JS runtime.

      Parameters:
      name - the theme name (e.g. "amiga")
      Returns:
      the whole .puml theme file as a string, or null if not present

    • hasThemes

      public static boolean hasThemes()
      Whether the PLANTUML_THEMES map exists at all, regardless of its content.

      This is what distinguishes "themes.js was never loaded", which is a problem with the page's deployment, from "themes.js is loaded but has no theme of that name", which is a typo in the diagram text.

    • getRaw_PLANTUML_STDLIB_INFO

      public static org.teavm.jso.JSObject getRaw_PLANTUML_STDLIB_INFO(String namespace)
      Retrieves the JSON info object for a loaded stdlib library.

      This reads from window.PLANTUML_STDLIB_INFO[namespace], which is populated by the generated JS files with metadata from each library's README.md YAML header (name, version, etc.).

      Parameters:
      namespace - the library name (e.g. "aws", "c4")
      Returns:
      the JS info object, or null if not found

    • getObjectKeys

      public static String getObjectKeys(org.teavm.jso.JSObject obj)
      Returns the keys of a JS object as a comma-separated string.

      Useful for iterating over properties of a JSObject from Java side, since TeaVM does not allow direct enumeration of JS object keys.

      Parameters:
      obj - a JS object
      Returns:
      comma-separated keys, or empty string if null/empty
